content.value_statement: Teams often struggle to keep UI decisions consistent across products. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code reusable design system guidance.
actual_capabilities: Defines design token categories for color, typography, spacing, radius, and shadow.
Explains atomic component architecture with common UI component examples.
Provides React and TypeScript component templates with props, variants, accessibility, and documentation sections.
Includes WCAG 2.1 AA guidance for contrast, keyboard navigation, ARIA, and screen readers.
Supplies a checklist for auditing tokens, components, patterns, documentation, testing, and governance.
limitations: Does not install dependencies or run build tools by itself.
Examples use React and TypeScript conventions and may need adaptation for other stacks.
Design tokens are starter examples and require brand-specific decisions.
Accessibility guidance supports reviews but does not replace manual testing with assistive technology.

use_cases.title: Start a New Design System
use_cases.description: Create a practical foundation for tokens, components, documentation, and accessibility standards.

use_cases.title: Standardize Frontend Components
use_cases.description: Use consistent component APIs, variants, and documentation patterns across an application.

use_cases.title: Audit Existing UI Standards
use_cases.description: Review tokens, patterns, accessibility, testing, governance, and adoption gaps with a structured checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Token Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new product interface.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me define a starter design token plan for a web application. Include color, typography, spacing, radius, and shadow decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Component API
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a reusable Button component API for a design system. Include variants, sizes, states, accessibility requirements, and documentation notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of a component already in development.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component against design system standards. Check token usage, prop naming, accessibility behavior, documentation, and test coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Migration Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced rollout across multiple product teams.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration strategy from inconsistent UI patterns to a shared design system. Include governance, adoption stages, documentation, and deprecation planning.

output_examples.input: A team needs a first design system plan for a SaaS dashboard.
output_examples.output: A structured plan covering token categories, core components, accessibility requirements, documentation setup, and adoption milestones.

output_examples.input: A developer wants to standardize a reusable input component.
output_examples.output: A component specification with prop guidance, states, accessibility behavior, examples to document, and testing notes.

output_examples.input: A design systems lead needs to audit an existing component library.
output_examples.output: A checklist-based review summary that highlights gaps in tokens, consistency, accessibility, documentation, tests, and governance.

best_practices: Start with semantic design tokens before building large component sets.
Document each component with purpose, variants, props, accessibility notes, and examples.
Test keyboard navigation, contrast, focus states, and screen reader behavior during implementation.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding one-off colors, spacing, and typography inside components.
Creating many component props when composition would be simpler.
Treating accessibility checks as a final review instead of a design requirement.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you plan design tokens, component architecture, documentation, accessibility standards, and audit workflows.

faq.question: Can it create production-ready components?
faq.answer: It provides templates and examples, but you must adapt and test them inside your application.

faq.question: Does it support accessibility work?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes WCAG 2.1 AA guidance for contrast, keyboard access, ARIA, and screen reader support.

faq.question: Which frontend stack is emphasized?
faq.answer: The examples emphasize React and TypeScript, with concepts that can transfer to other component frameworks.

faq.question: Can it help improve an existing system?
faq.answer: Yes. The checklist can guide audits of tokens, components, patterns, documentation, testing, and governance.

faq.question: Does it connect to external services?
faq.answer: No. The files provide documentation, templates, and references without runtime service integration.
